1 # Gandalf
2 
3 **One sentence:** A deep-think second opinion on any artifact or effort — what’s really going on, what’s wrong or missing, how it sits vs best-in-class, and what problems are coming.
4 
5 ## Use this when
6 - You want a rigorous read: “what am I missing?”
7 - Stakes are high and a polite rubber-stamp review is useless
8 - You need diagnosis + situating + foresight, not just a list of nits
9 
10 ## Do not use this when
11 - You need new ideas generated (use Jumper)
12 - You need multi-plan planning to convergence (use Crucible)
13 - You need claim verification research as the main product (use researchPrime)
14 
15 ## What you get
16 - A structured diagnosis ranked by consequence (and “this is sound” when it is)
17 - Situating against better-known solutions when warranted
18 - Forward-looking “coming problems” with honest risk labels
19 - Confidence tiers earned by independent checks — not self-awarded gold stars
20 
21 ## What it is not
22 - Not a brainstorm generator
23 - Not a builder or planner
24 - Not free to claim “proven” without independent refutation work
25 
26 ## How to start (human)
27 1. Point Gandalf at the document, plan, code, or effort in question.
28 2. Say what decision you’re trying to make (or what “good” looks like).
29 3. Prefer the deeper path for medium/high stakes; accept lighter stamps when stakes are low.
30 4. Act on grounded findings first; treat speculative ones as hypotheses.
31 
32 ## Limits (honest)
33 - Independent cross-check paths may be unavailable; then stamps stay conservative and say so
34 - It elevates insight, not flattery — operator preferences can be challenged
35 - Large whole-repo reads may need an explicit scale path
36 
37 ## For agents / engines
38 Full protocol and wiring live in `SKILL.md` next to this file. Load that only when running the skill — this card is for people.
